title: How many times is locker twelve flipped, and how does it end?
description: In the locker puzzle of {{NAME_1}}, the video finds who flips locker twelve by pairing its factors, then decides if it ends open or closed. Keeko doubts the count after listing the factors and leaving out twelve itself.
teaching_notes: One idea: a locker is flipped once for each factor of its number, and factors come in pairs. The video ends with Keeko missing the number itself as a factor. Watch for students who list the factors below the number and forget the number.

source: How many times is locker 12 toggled, and does it end open or closed?
video_script.why: The child sees that the number of people who flip a locker is its number of factors, and that an even count leaves the locker closed.
video_script.substitution: List the factors of the locker number in pairs, count them, and ask if the count is even or odd.
video_script.anchor: the row of closed lockers of {{NAME_1}} in the kingdom of Khoisnam
video_script.wrong_answer: five times, so it ends open
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko lists one, two, three, four and six, forgets twelve itself, and says five times, so it ends open. Person twelve flips it too, so the count is six.
video_script.payoff_line: Locker twelve is flipped six times, so it ends closed

final_answer.spoken: six times, so it ends closed

names.{{NAME_1}}: the queen of Khoisnam whose will hides the treasure in one of 100 lockers

never_show: the answer to the exercise video about the first five lockers touched twice
maths_rules: all lockers start closed; person k toggles every locker whose number is a multiple of k
locker 12 is toggled by person k exactly when k divides 12
6 toggles is even: closed, open, closed, open, closed, open, closed; it ends closed
the slip: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 is only 5 factors; 12 itself is missing
video_script.design: One idea: flips equal factors, and factors pair up. Wrong idea: forgetting the number itself. The row of lockers stays in the anchor band.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a row of closed lockers in the anchor band, numbered 1 to 12 and more; locker 12 has a ring round it and an empty box for how many flips and open or closed

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.row: a row of closed lockers appears, numbered from 1
marks.flip: one locker door swings open and shut to show a toggle
marks.walk: person 1 walks along the whole row, then person 2 along every second locker

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='row'/>{{NAME_1}} left a long row of lockers, all of them closed.
<bookmark mark='flip'/>To toggle a locker means to flip it, from closed to open or from open to closed.
<bookmark mark='walk'/>Person one toggles every locker. Person two toggles every second locker, and so on.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many times is locker twelve toggled, and does it end open or closed?

beats.on_screen: the question holds still and locker 12 gets an accent underline

marks.stop: locker 12 is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the lockers grow on the stage; person 1 walks past and flips locker 12; person 2 flips every second locker and reaches 12; person 5 walks past 10 and skips 12; the rule card k divides 12 appears

marks.two: person 2 flips every second locker and lands on 12
marks.five: person 5 skips locker 12 and it stays still
marks.rule: the rule card k divides 12 appears

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Person one flips locker twelve, because one goes into twelve.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Person two stops at two, four, six and so on, and twelve is on that list.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Person five stops at five, ten and fifteen, so locker twelve is skipped.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Locker twelve is flipped only by people whose number divides twelve exactly.

beats.on_screen: Given: 100 lockers, all closed. Person k toggles every k-th locker. Locker 12.

marks.given: the three given facts are written one under the other

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, every locker starts closed, and person after person toggles the lockers along the row.

beats.on_screen: To find: how many times locker 12 is toggled, and open or closed

marks.find: the two things to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how many times locker twelve is toggled, and how it ends.

marks.pairs: 1 × 12 appears with an arc joining the pair

narration: <bookmark mark='pairs'/>Step one, find the factors of twelve in pairs, starting with one times twelve.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Two times six is twelve, and three times four is twelve as well.

beats.on_screen: Factors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12; that is 6 factors, so 6 people

marks.line: the six factors line up in a row
marks.count: the six factors are counted one by one

narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>Step two, line up the factors. They are one, two, three, four, six and twelve.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Three pairs give six factors, so six people flip this locker.

beats.on_screen: closed, open, closed, open, closed, open, closed

marks.door: the locker door swings once for each person and the states are listed

narration: <bookmark mark='door'/>Step three, flip the door once for each person, starting from closed.
Every two flips bring the door back to closed, and six flips is an even number.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Locker 12 is toggled 6 times, so it ends closed
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Locker twelve is flipped six times, so it ends closed.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6; the factor 12 is missing and then glows

marks.fix: twelve joins the list and the count becomes six

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks locker twelve is flipped five times, so it ends open.
<bookmark mark='miss'/>Keeko listed one, two, three, four and six, and left out twelve itself.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Person twelve flips locker twelve too. Every number is a factor of itself.
